title: Introduce fragmentation valve and KV tombstone regulator to stop GPU OOM cascade
creator: Aisha Roy
description: Production incidents across Hosted/Dedicated/Private clusters caused recurring GPU OOMs correlated with KV cache index bloat and slow allocator coalescing. Multiple customers reported sustained request failures and elevated latency during long-tail workloads; initial triage pointed to a class of micro-fragmentation that escalated into hard OOMs under bursty multi-tenant traffic. Goal: ship a staged runtime patch that prevents immediate customer impact, adds safe fallbacks, and reduces long-term index/tombstone growth.
root_cause: Under sustained mixed-size prefix allocations the arena allocator failed to coalesce freed slabs due to a race between async journal compaction and eviction; concurrently KV index tombstones were retained longer than necessary (grace period calibration bug), causing metadata bloat that prevented efficient reuse of GPU pages. The combined effect produced allocation denial despite nominal free memory.
mitigation_steps: Implemented fragmentation-valve: per-tenant adaptive slab reclaimer that triggers incremental compaction when fragmentation ratio crosses threshold
Lowered KV tombstone retention window and added aggressive compaction during high write churn
Backported emergency soft-fallback to CPU-hosted generation for tenants hitting OOM to keep requests alive while preserving fairness
Added allocation-time hot-check to avoid irreversible GPU allocation failure and instead perform controlled slow-path handling
Deployed runtime metrics to Datadog for fragmentation ratio, tombstone-queue-length, and per-tenant evict-pressure
resolution_summary: Patch runtime v1.20 rolled out via canary -> small percentage tenants -> global. Immediate customer impact dropped to near zero within first hour on canaries. No regressions observed in throughput; latency spike during compaction window within acceptable SLO. GitHub PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218 contains the core allocator changes and unit tests. Rollout notes and dashboards are documented in Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: No new GPU OOM escalations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private for 72h post-rollout
Fragmentation ratio reduced by >=60% on affected hosts within 30 minutes of valve activation
KV tombstone queue length returns to baseline on high-churn tenants within 1 hour
Fallback path successfully serves requests for at least 99% of retries in canary group

next_steps: Schedule allocator design session to evaluate long-term fragmentation-resistant allocator rewrite
Introduce tenant-level TTL tuning knobs exposed in Console with guardrails
Add synthetic long-tail workload CI test to catch similar regressions pre-release
Follow up with affected customers and include mitigation details in transparency report
postmortem_notes: Immediate fix prevented further escalations. Contributing factors: insufficient compaction frequency under mixed-size workloads, tombstone grace period mismatch between indexer and eviction loop, and lack of a safe fallback path prior to this work. Ownership for index compaction and allocator maintenance assigned to Runtime Allocations squad.
